**Service denied:** Neck (cervical) fusion (ACDF), CPT 22551
**Governing policy:** PH Medical Policy 91581-R23 SPINE PROCEDURES — https://priorityhealth.stylelabs.cloud/api/public/content/5f005b3ee3044b68ad920d57974c2d68?v=785108c8

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing Priority Health's decision to deny prior authorization for the cervical fusion (ACDF, CPT 22551) requested by my surgeon. The notice dated 2026-08-01 states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking Priority Health to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery. My surgeon, Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery, has documented that this procedure is needed.

## The plan's own policy covers this procedure

The medical policy that governs my request, PH Medical Policy 91581-R23 SPINE PROCEDURES, states:

> "Cervical Spine Fusion procedures are medically necessary according to TurningPoint criteria."

So the procedure I am asking for is not excluded by my plan and is not considered experimental. Under the plan's own language, whether it is covered turns on a set of clinical criteria that Priority Health has delegated to TurningPoint.

I want to be straightforward with you about one thing: **the TurningPoint criteria that were actually applied to my case have not been quoted to me, and I am not quoting them here.** The sentence above is the plan language I have. Everything that follows is my own description of what my medical records show.

## What my records show

The prior authorization packet my surgeon submitted documents the following:

- **Duration of symptoms:** 18 months of progressive neck pain that is not relieved by rest.
- **Supervised conservative care:** 10 weeks of supervised physical therapy, including cervical traction and postural training, from 2026-04-12 to 2026-06-21, with 18 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trial:** NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief.
- **Injection trial:** a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-22, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging:** MRI of the cervical spine on 2026-05-20 showing a C5-C6 disc herniation with severe right foraminal narrowing and C6 nerve root compression.
- **Symptoms and function:** radicular pain and numbness into the right thumb and index finger, with weakness.
- **Physical exam:** positive provocative testing on the affected side, and a neurologic deficit that corresponds to the level seen on the MRI.
- **Surgical risk factors:** no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

In plain terms: the imaging identifies a specific problem at a specific level, my exam findings match that level, and I tried therapy, medication, and an injection first without lasting relief. My surgeon reviewed all of this and documented that the fusion is needed.

## Request for the criteria that were applied

Because the policy points to an outside criteria set rather than spelling out the clinical rules, I am asking Priority Health, as part of this appeal, to **provide me in writing, free of charge, the specific TurningPoint criteria applied to CPT 22551 in my case, and the specific criterion or criteria the reviewer found were not met.** Priority Health and its delegate hold these criteria; I do not. I am requesting them through the criteria request form on the policy page and through Priority Health's Prism portal under Authorizations > Authorization Criteria Lookup. I also ask for the name and specialty of the reviewer who made this determination. Without seeing the rule I am said to have failed, I cannot fully respond to it, and I ask that the record reflect that I requested it.

If any item in my chart is missing or unclear to the reviewer, I ask that Priority Health contact my surgeon's office directly rather than close the appeal on an incomplete file.

## What I am asking for

I ask Priority Health to overturn the denial dated 2026-08-01 and authorize the cervical fusion (ACDF, CPT 22551) requested by Dr. Marchetti. I understand this is Level 1 of Priority Health's three-level process, which ends with Michigan's external review, and I intend to use each level available to me if needed.

**Appeal deadline and submission:** This appeal must be received by **2027-01-28**, within 180 days of the 2026-08-01 adverse determination. I am submitting it to Priority Health by one of the plan's accepted methods — the online appeal form on priorityhealth.com, email to phmemberappeals@priorityhealth.com, mail to Priority Health, 1231 East Beltline Ave. NE, Grand Rapids, MI 49525-4501, fax to 616-975-8894, or verbally through Customer Service at the number on the back of my membership card. I understand that if this appeal is not resolved in my favor, a Level 2 appeal is due within 90 days and a state external review within 127 days, and that the deadlines stated in my denial letter are authoritative.

Please send your decision in writing to the address above. Thank you for taking a careful second look at my file.

Sincerely,

**Skyler Mercado**
